resources.title: My then and now record
paragraphs_in_document_order: Thursday 11 February 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Teach a forty-minute assessing lesson for three to four pupils. Reuse the invented town scenes from Week 4. Each pupil makes a two-panel then-and-now record of one place, with one caption per panel. Supplied pictures or drawings stand in for photos. Keep all usual scaffolds available.

BUILD Weekly - Spring!B45/C45: Record 'then & now' with photos/captions. Theme: Resilience & Change. Unit, BUILD - Spring!D10: Then & now, how things change. Term assessment context, J10: F: ordering tasks.  S: personal timeline produced.

This is the assessing week under the owner brief. The weekly outcome and six-week grid define this return; the quoted term assessment remains source context. Success: one matched invented place pair, then left/now right, and a relevant caption for each panel. Do not assess artistic skill, independent handwriting or reading aloud.

Set Source Cards, Support Cards, word mat, books and drawing tools at each place. Starter: match the park views and find the tree in both. Prepare spare copies for one selected column per pupil. Adult cuts along white gaps if wanted; pupils can draw instead. Keep a full labelled sheet beside the cut pair.

Every task keeps a word bank, sentence starters and visible model. Level 2 describes the requested scaffolds, not a qualification level. Supported, Independent and Aspire retain them throughout assessment. Exact scribing and usual communication aids are available. No public questioning, cold calling or required reading aloud.

All scenes and changes are invented, reused unchanged from Week 4. They are not records of actual local history. Use park, high street or bus stop only as type words. No real people, places, events, buildings or historical dates are represented. No live research, personal photographs or personal disclosure is required.
My then and now record continued
Thursday 11 February 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A
2 minutes private settle; 8 minutes match park views and find a shared clue. Check earlier book evidence privately if available.
5 minutes source learning with brief reset; 5 minutes two-panel model and private hinge; 5 minutes choose pair, mode and caption words.
10 minutes make record, including brief reset; 3 minutes private caption check and response; 2 minutes exit and evidence.

“These places are made up. We can use these pictures or draw them. I put then on the left and now on the right. Each picture needs words that fit it. Then there was no bench. Now there is a bench.” Point to each park view. “You choose your pair and words. I can help you write.”

“Now there is a bench” fits which park view? The now view. If unsure, trace the empty space then and the bench now; re-pair the caption. Parallel check: “Now there is a shelter” fits the now bus-stop view. Keep the model and banks available. A prompt does not automatically mean an outcome is not shown.

Pupil chooses a pair, points to the clue and selects caption words for each panel. Short phrases such as “Then no bench” and “Now a bench” are valid. Adult writes exact selected meaning, reads back quietly and offers keep/change. Record adult contribution and pupil confirmation. Model copying alone does not establish understanding.

Use pictures or drawing in books. Adult cuts cards; optional touch. HELP/PASS, quiet request, supported observation or an agreed supervised pause remain available. Use quiet wait time, usual aids and planning in any language. No camera, device or trip needed.
My then and now record continued
Thursday 11 February 2027 | P3 | 40 minutes | Year A

Supported: choose and place/draw one pair, select caption words and direct a scribe. Independent: make two panels and two captions with all scaffolds. Aspire: after the shared finish, add a same feature or a question about the past. Every route finishes with one picture/drawing and one caption in each labelled panel.

Cognition: one pair and one caption at a time. Communication: pointing, usual aid, short stems and exact scribe. SEMH: predictable steps and private feedback. Sensory/physical: large pictures, adult cutting and drawing choice. Words, shape, position and borders carry meaning without colour.

Use Evidence Sheet page 2 separately for each pupil. It lists all six outcomes verbatim from rows 40–45. For each row tick S shown, P part shown, N not yet shown after a fair supported chance, or U not seen/no evidence. Comment with date/book reference, what was observed and actual support. Use earlier records or a brief private check; never infer all six outcomes from today’s two-panel piece. If evidence is absent, leave the judgement at U and note a future check, not failure.

Evidence HUM-BUILD-S1-W06-E1: chosen pair, both captions, confirmation and support. Actual audience reply, one NS and the pupil’s response in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode precede R; E follows actual banking. Attendance, responses and all grid judgements remain blank until used. Absent pupils remain blank.

A collections worker keeps pictures and captions to record change. Offer authentic pupil choices and words to the Communication portfolio. [AWARD] / [QUAL] checks remain separate.

Top then, bottom now. Left high street, middle park, right bus stop. All places and changes invented. Label then left and now right in the finished book record. Accept short phrases that preserve the meaning, not just the full model sentences.

“Now there is a bench” matches the now park view. If unsure, trace the space without a bench then the bench and re-pair the caption. Parallel check: “Now there is a shelter” matches the now bus-stop view. Keep the banks, starters and visible model. Drawing skill and spelling are not the outcome.

Shops, tree/path and stop pole/fence stay in the paired scenes. No real place, building, person, event or exact date is shown. The earlier/later context is supplied fiction. S shown; P part; N not yet; U not seen.
Keep missing evidence distinct from not yet.

Adult assessment brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Hidden adult brief: Level2 means bank, starters and visible model every task, not a qualification level. Prompt ladder point, short private prompt, rephrase, choice/scaffold, model first step then return. Pupil number: ____; no real people, places or events as subjects. Grid S shown, P part shown, N not yet shown after a fair supported chance, U not seen/no evidence. One per pupil. Comment with date/reference, what was seen and actual help. No retrospective invented evidence or automatic award decisions.
